sources.entry: Building the CoreWiki This is a Wiki-style content management system that has been completely written in C# with ASP.NET Core and Razor Pages. You can find the source code here.

summary.one_liner: CoreWiki is a simple wiki-style content management system written in C# with ASP.NET Core and Razor Pages, built during live coding streams as a learning project.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a wiki where users can create, view, edit, and delete articles that have a topic, published date, and content. Articles can be listed as the latest 10 changes (ordered by published date) or as all articles (ordered by topic). Logged-in users can add comments on article detail pages. A default HomePage article is shown when no topic is specified, and unknown URLs show a NotFound page. The README also mentions search-engine-friendly URLs, though that section has only a placeholder description. Setup uses npm and dotnet, and a first-run start wizard creates a default administrator account in newer versions.
use_cases: studying a C# web app built on live streams
contributing to an open-source ASP.NET Core project
how_to_run: Optional: dotnet watch run to rebuild on code changes
notable: Built live on Jeff Fritz's coding streams, with a public recordings index and workshop series
Runs on Windows, Mac, Linux, and in a container, according to the README
Includes a Deploy to Azure button for quick deployment
Built and tested continuously with Azure Pipelines
Contribution guide and help-wanted issues aimed at newcomers
caveats: Described as a basic project; features are a simple checklist rather than a full-featured wiki
The README's live demo link is empty, and the Deploy to Azure link is not shown in the text
Some feature sections are placeholders (for example, the search-friendly URL and error sections)
Requires both Node.js with npm and the .NET Core SDK
